⚡️ Iran stresses international transit facilitation at Geneva transport meeting

📌 London, IRNA – Iran has stressed the need to harmonize border and customs procedures to reduce the time and cost of international transit at a United Nations transport meeting in Geneva.

Mehran Ghorbani, deputy minister of roads and urban development, outlined Iran’s views on developing transport corridors and improving the efficiency of transit networks at a panel during the 39th session of the UNECE Working Party on Transport Trends and Economics (WP.5) in Geneva on Wednesday.
​
Ghorbani said Iran viewed its location along the International North-South Transport Corridor and east-west routes not only as a geographical advantage but also as a responsibility to provide safe, efficient and continuous transit for the region and beyond.
​
He identified completion of strategic infrastructure, including the Chabahar-Zahedan and Rasht-Astara railway lines, as key priorities for strengthening interregional connectivity.
​
Ghorbani also called for harmonized customs and border procedures, standardized documents and secure, reliable data exchange between national systems to reduce border waiting times and transport costs while making transit routes more predictable.
​
He also highlighted Iran’s efforts to facilitate data exchange among customs, trade and transport authorities and the use of smart technologies, stressing the potential of international instruments and standards, including the TIR Convention, to facilitate international transport.

📡 Baqaei recalls Minab school martyrs on first day of new school year

📌 Tehran, IRNA – Foreign Ministry Spokesperson Esmaeil Baqaei has marked the first day of the new school year by honoring the memory of the Minab school students massacared in a US-Israeli attack, saying the angels of Minab will forever remain in the hearts of Iranians.

In a post on his X account on Wednesday, marking the start of the new school year and honoring the Minab students by posting photos of them, Baqaei wrote, “Today is the first day of Mehr, the day Iranian schools reopen, and these are the innocent faces of the children of #Minab, martyred in the savage American Tomahawk missile attack of 28 February.”
​
He noted, “They should have been here today, bright-eyed and joyful, celebrating the start of a new school year.”
​
“Instead, their slain bodies lie buried in the earth”, he added.
​
Baqaei added, “The government whose president mockingly flouts international law from the UN podium bears responsibility for this unforgivable war crime.”
​
Stressing, “All who stood silent and looked away share in that responsibility.”
​
“The Iranian people will never forget these angelic faces. They will never forgive their killers,” he emphasized.

📲 @Irna_en​
